## Overview

Let FlashInfer select the Kimi-K3 fused KDA T=1 decode kernel: with `kda_decode_backend="flashinfer"` and a FlashInfer whose `fused_kda_decode` accepts them, pass `backend="auto"` and `state_indices_mode="unique_or_null"`; on the pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` FlashInfer receives the same arguments as before. No new environment variable, module or Cake-specific logic in vLLM. Related tracker: #59725; FlashInfer side: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4967.

## Claims

* With `kda_decode_backend="flashinfer"` and a FlashInfer whose `fused_kda_decode` accepts `backend` / `state_indices_mode` (FlashInfer >= 0.7.1rc1, added by flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4967), the Kimi-K3 KDA T=1 decode call passes `backend="auto"` and `state_indices_mode="unique_or_null"`, and FlashInfer selects the kernel (on SM100 / SM103 its generated Cake variants where a route matches, the CuTe DSL kernel otherwise). vLLM carries no Cake-specific logic, switch or module.
* On FlashInfer builds without the two parameters (the pinned `0.7.0.post1`) FlashInfer receives the same arguments as before (the call site now goes through a helper that forwards an empty kwargs dict); the other KDA decode backends are untouched.
* Validation: 12 CPU dispatch tests, the existing GPU correctness test (13 passed / 7 test-own skips) and a kernel-selection probe on one B200; end to end on Kimi-K3 NVFP4 TP8 (two GB300 nodes): GSM8K 0.945 (native) vs 0.943 (`auto`), serving throughput and medians within ±1.5 % of native, one run per arm.

## Validation

The unit tests, the GPU correctness test and the kernel-selection probe ran on single B200 (SM100) nodes inside the vLLM `cu134` nightly image (vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev23+g43b4aaea3.d20261007, torch 2.15.0.dev20260928+cu134, nvcc 13.4) with this branch's files overlaid: the GPU test and the probe each on one B200, the CPU tests in GPU-less steps. For the GPU test and the probe, `flashinfer-python 0.7.1rc5` (a release with the two parameters) was installed as a pure-Python wheel into a private directory that shadows the image's pinned 0.7.0.post1, so the probe was true there; the probe-false path (pinned wheel, same arguments as before) is the one CI exercises, see below. The GPU test and the probe ran on the revision before the announcement fix; the commits since touch only the announcement (two small helpers that render the kwargs to a `k=v` string before `logger.info_once`), its CPU test and three docstrings. The end-to-end run is on GB300 (SM103) and is described in its own paragraph.

**Unit tests (CPU, `cpu_test`)** `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_flashinfer_decode_dispatch.py`, 12 cases, **12 passed** (run with 0.7.1rc5 installed; the 11 cases that predate the announcement test also passed with the pinned 0.7.0.post1). The cases monkeypatch the availability check, the module lookup and the FlashInfer function, so they do not depend on the installed FlashInfer:

* the signature check accepts a `fused_kda_decode` with `backend` / `state_indices_mode`, rejects one without them and a non-callable;
* the cached probe follows the installed signature and is false when FlashInfer has no fused decode at all;
* `_flashinfer_fused_kda_decode` passes `backend="auto"` and `state_indices_mode="unique_or_null"` only when the probe is true (and neither key otherwise), forwarding the tensors unchanged;
* the init decision is empty for `native` / `triton` and for `flashinfer` without the probe, and the two kwargs for `flashinfer` with it;
* `KimiK3DeltaAttention._forward` keeps its `@eager_break_during_capture` decorator;
* the once-only announcement of the selected call renders its kwargs to a string before `logger.info_once` hashes them (the previous revision passed the dict itself, which raised `TypeError: unhashable type` while constructing every KDA layer; the end-to-end run below caught it, fixed in the announcement-fix commit).

**GPU correctness** `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py -k fused_kda_decode_correctness` with 0.7.1rc5 on one B200: **13 passed, 7 skipped**: all 10 `native` cases and 3 of the 10 `flashinfer` cases pass; the other 7 `flashinfer` cases are the test's own skips (FlashInfer's fused decode always applies the output norm and requires the `SD` conv-state layout, `(state_len, dim)`). The `flashinfer` cases now pass the same kwargs helper result to the direct `flashinfer_fused_kda_decode` call, so they exercise the `auto` selection. CI: both test files run in the B200 Kimi K3 step (`tests/models/kimi_k3/`); because CI pins `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` it exercises the probe-false path (same arguments as before); the `auto` path is covered by the B200 and GB300 runs here until the pin moves.

**Which kernel `auto` selects.** A probe that mirrors the test's inputs (bf16 recurrent state, SD conv layout; 11 cases: H = 12 with 1 row / lb = −5 / the test's padded row strides, 4 rows / lb = None / padded, 1 row / lb = −5 / contiguous, 4 rows / lb = −5 / contiguous, 4 rows / lb = None / contiguous; then contiguous, lb = −5 for H = 24 × 4 rows, H = 32 × 1 and 4 rows, H = 48 × 4 rows, H = 96 × 1 and 4 rows) and counts FlashInfer's Cake launches: on B200 every one of the 11 `auto` calls ran a Cake fused-decode variant (`wide512_bf16`; `direct_bf16` at H = 48 × 4 rows; `compact_async_bf16` at H = 96 × 4 rows). Each output is within the BF16 tolerance (atol = rtol = 1e-2) of the vLLM reference (`causal_conv1d_update` + `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` + the fused output norm); max |Δ| vs the reference < 4e-3, vs the CuTe-DSL kernel on identical inputs < 4e-3, recurrent-state Δ < 2.5e-4, conv state identical. These are the bf16-state variants; the serving run below selects the fp32-state variants (vLLM keeps the KDA recurrent state in fp32), whose evidence is the end-to-end result. The probe script is not part of this PR; I can attach it on request.

**End to end (`nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4`, served from a local copy with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`; TP8 over two GB300 nodes, SM103).** Two `vllm serve` arms on the same image, FlashInfer build and checkpoint (vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d.d20261006 nightly, cu134; FlashInfer built from `main` at https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9eb882ad346d8ec8a18dca2f1cba4c7095b740c9, which has the two parameters; `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --distributed-executor-backend ray --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --trust-remote-code --attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"mla_prefill_backend":"flashinfer"}'`): **native** (defaults: vLLM's own KDA decode) and **fiauto** (`--additional-config '{"kda_decode_backend":"flashinfer"}'`, i.e. FlashInfer's `fused_kda_decode(backend="auto", state_indices_mode="unique_or_null")`). One run per arm, no repeats, so differences below a few percent are within noise.

* *Correctness.* GSM8K test set, all 1319 questions through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` endpoint at 64-way concurrency (a port of sglang's `few_shot_gsm8k` to `/v1/completions`: 5 shots, greedy, 512 max new tokens, stop on `["Question", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"]`, last-integer scoring; the client script is not part of this PR, available on request): native **0.945**, fiauto **0.943** (unparseable answers 0.1 % vs 0.2 %); 0 request errors; wall time 251 s vs 255 s. That is a 2 to 3 question difference from one greedy run per arm; the two kernels accumulate differently, so token-identical outputs are not expected, and no repeats were run to put a band on it.
* *Serving.* `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos` (1024-token prompts, 128 output tokens unless stated), median / p99 in ms:

  | scenario | arm | req/s | out tok/s | TTFT med / p99 | TPOT med / p99 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 200 prompts, concurrency 32 | native | 7.10 | 909 | 797 / 1337 | 27.30 / 31.49 |
  |  | fiauto | 7.05 | 902 | 796 / 1330 | 27.45 / 31.70 |
  | 32 prompts, concurrency 32 (warm-up pass, run first) | native | 7.39 | 946 | 1069 / 1496 | 25.51 / 30.38 |
  |  | fiauto | 7.36 | 942 | 1066 / 1494 | 25.66 / 30.53 |
  | 32 prompts, concurrency 8 | native | 3.22 | 413 | 506 / 553 | 15.47 / 17.72 |
  |  | fiauto | 3.24 | 415 | 505 / 535 | 15.40 / 17.60 |
  | 8 prompts, concurrency 1 | native | 0.611 | 78.2 | 225 / 256 | 11.06 / 11.12 |
  |  | fiauto | 0.615 | 78.7 | 223 / 231 | 11.05 / 11.11 |
  | 4 prompts of 8192 tokens, 16 output, concurrency 1 | native | 1.85 | 29.6 | 351 / 419 | 11.40 / 11.63 |
  |  | fiauto | 1.84 | 29.4 | 352 / 428 | 11.57 / 11.72 |

  Throughput, median TTFT and median / p99 TPOT are within ±1.5 % of native in every scenario (largest +1.48 %, the 8192-token TPOT median); p99 TTFT moves by −3.1 % at concurrency 8, −9.7 % at concurrency 1 and +2.1 % for the 8192-token prompts, single-run tail values over 4 to 32 requests (deltas from the unrounded values; the table rounds). With one run per arm this is no regression signal and no measurable end-to-end gain at these shapes; the KDA decode's share of the per-token time was not profiled. Commands:

  ```
  # MODEL = local copy of nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:PORT --model $MODEL --served-model-name k3 --tokenizer $MODEL --trust-remote-code \
    --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \
    --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 32     # warm-up pass, run first
  # then, same flags with: --num-prompts 200 --max-concurrency 32 | --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 | --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1
  # and: --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 16 --num-prompts 4 --max-concurrency 1   (default seed)
  ```
* *Which kernel ran.* The fiauto server log carries 32 FlashInfer JIT lines `Generated Cake fused KDA decode <variant> sm103a JIT spec` for four fp32-state variants (`wide512_f32`, `direct_f32`, `compact_async_f32`, `high_work_f32`), i.e. `auto` selected and compiled them at first use (the count matches one set per rank); the native log has no such line and no `fused_kda_decode` mention at all. The layer's own once-only INFO announcement was not found in the collected API-server log, so the JIT lines are the evidence.
* The native arm ran on the revision before the announcement fix; the fiauto arm is the rerun on the announcement-fix revision (the first fiauto attempt failed at model construction). The two revisions differ only in the announcement helpers and their test; the head since adds only a docstring correction (the FlashInfer version that carries the two parameters).

## Details

This PR started as an opt-in `VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES` change (its first commit) and was reworked after maintainer feedback that vLLM should carry no awareness of Cake-generated kernels (Cake: the generated kernel family inside FlashInfer that `backend="auto"` can select for these Kimi-K3 shapes). On the current head the `VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES` switch, the host-side admission predicates and the Kimi-K3 MLA decode route are gone; the net diff against `main` is the four files below. Kernel selection is FlashInfer's job.

### What changes

* `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py`
  * `_flashinfer_kda_decode_kwargs(backend)` decides once, at layer init, which extra kwargs the FlashInfer call gets: `{"backend": "auto", "state_indices_mode": "unique_or_null"}` when `backend == "flashinfer"` and the probe below is true, `{}` otherwise. The result is stored as `self.flashinfer_kda_decode_kwargs`; when non-empty, `_announce_flashinfer_kda_decode` logs it once (INFO) after `_format_kda_decode_kwargs` has rendered it to a `k=v, ...` string.
  * The FlashInfer decode call moves into `KimiK3DeltaAttention._flashinfer_fused_kda_decode(...)`, which forwards `**self.flashinfer_kda_decode_kwargs`. The branch condition in `_forward` (the FlashInfer path is taken exactly when it was before, only for `kda_decode_backend == "flashinfer"`), the `auto` / `native` / `triton` / `flashinfer` resolution and the `@eager_break_during_capture` decorator are unchanged; the call itself now goes through the helper and gains the two kwargs.
  * Module constant `_FLASHINFER_KDA_STATE_INDICES_MODE = "unique_or_null"` with the rationale below.
* `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`
  * `flashinfer_fused_kda_decode_selects_backend()` (cached): true when FlashInfer's `fused_kda_decode` is available and its signature accepts `backend` and `state_indices_mode`. `_fused_kda_decode_accepts_backend(fn)` is the signature check.
* Tests: `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_flashinfer_decode_dispatch.py` (new, CPU) and a two-line change in `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py`. The earlier form's `tests/v1/attention/test_cake_routes_kimi_k3.py` no longer exists on this branch (not part of the net diff).

### FlashInfer semantics relied on

In FlashInfer `main` (`flashinfer/kda_decode.py`), `fused_kda_decode(..., backend="auto", state_indices_mode=...)`:

* `backend="auto"` selects FlashInfer's Cake-generated program only when `state_indices_mode` is supplied and one of its routes matches the call (SM100a / SM103a, a matching layout); otherwise it runs the CuTe DSL kernel, i.e. the same kernel the call ran before this PR.
* `state_indices_mode` is consumed only by that selector; it is a host-side statement about the `state_indices` tensor, never verified on the device.

**Version note.** The two parameters exist in FlashInfer >= 0.7.1rc1 (every 0.7.1 pre-release; added by flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4967). The pinned `0.7.0.post1` does not have them, the probe returns false and FlashInfer receives the same arguments as before; when the pin moves to a release with them, every `kda_decode_backend="flashinfer"` deployment switches to the `auto` form without further vLLM changes. That backend stays opt-in (vLLM's own decode is the default); inside it there is no vLLM knob to keep the CuTe DSL kernel, and FlashInfer has no environment switch for this call either, so the way back is another `kda_decode_backend`.

**Why `unique_or_null`.** vLLM's KDA metadata fills CUDA-graph padding rows with `NULL_BLOCK_ID` (0), the reserved null block owned by no request, and every live T=1 decode row owns its own block, so the state indices are non-positive or unique. FlashInfer treats non-positive rows as the null path (zero output, no state update). `positive_unique` would be a false assertion under padding. Because FlashInfer does not verify the mode on the device, it has to hold for every caller path that reaches the FlashInfer decode; the single call site in `_forward` is that path and it only runs for pure T=1 decode batches (`num_prefills == 0`, no speculative tokens).

## Details

This PR started as an opt-in `VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES` change (its first commit) and was reworked after maintainer feedback that vLLM should carry no awareness of Cake-generated kernels (Cake: the generated kernel family inside FlashInfer that `backend="auto"` can select for these Kimi-K3 shapes). On the current head the `VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES` switch, the host-side admission predicates and the Kimi-K3 MLA decode route are gone; the net diff against `main` is the four files below. Kernel selection is FlashInfer's job.

### What changes

* `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py`
  * `_flashinfer_kda_decode_kwargs(backend)` decides once, at layer init, which extra kwargs the FlashInfer call gets: `{"backend": "auto", "state_indices_mode": "unique_or_null"}` when `backend == "flashinfer"` and the probe below is true, `{}` otherwise. The result is stored as `self.flashinfer_kda_decode_kwargs`; when non-empty, `_announce_flashinfer_kda_decode` logs it once (INFO) after `_format_kda_decode_kwargs` has rendered it to a `k=v, ...` string.
  * The FlashInfer decode call moves into `KimiK3DeltaAttention._flashinfer_fused_kda_decode(...)`, which forwards `**self.flashinfer_kda_decode_kwargs`. The branch condition in `_forward` (the FlashInfer path is taken exactly when it was before, only for `kda_decode_backend == "flashinfer"`), the `auto` / `native` / `triton` / `flashinfer` resolution and the `@eager_break_during_capture` decorator are unchanged; the call itself now goes through the helper and gains the two kwargs.
  * Module constant `_FLASHINFER_KDA_STATE_INDICES_MODE = "unique_or_null"` with the rationale below.
* `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`
  * `flashinfer_fused_kda_decode_selects_backend()` (cached): true when FlashInfer's `fused_kda_decode` is available and its signature accepts `backend` and `state_indices_mode`. `_fused_kda_decode_accepts_backend(fn)` is the signature check.
* Tests: `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_flashinfer_decode_dispatch.py` (new, CPU) and a two-line change in `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py`. The earlier form's `tests/v1/attention/test_cake_routes_kimi_k3.py` no longer exists on this branch (not part of the net diff).

### FlashInfer semantics relied on

In FlashInfer `main` (`flashinfer/kda_decode.py`), `fused_kda_decode(..., backend="auto", state_indices_mode=...)`:

* `backend="auto"` selects FlashInfer's Cake-generated program only when `state_indices_mode` is supplied and one of its routes matches the call (SM100a / SM103a, a matching layout); otherwise it runs the CuTe DSL kernel, i.e. the same kernel the call ran before this PR.
* `state_indices_mode` is consumed only by that selector; it is a host-side statement about the `state_indices` tensor, never verified on the device.

**Version note.** The two parameters exist in FlashInfer >= 0.7.1rc1 (every 0.7.1 pre-release; added by flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4967). The pinned `0.7.0.post1` does not have them, the probe returns false and FlashInfer receives the same arguments as before; when the pin moves to a release with them, every `kda_decode_backend="flashinfer"` deployment switches to the `auto` form without further vLLM changes. That backend stays opt-in (vLLM's own decode is the default); inside it there is no vLLM knob to keep the CuTe DSL kernel, and FlashInfer has no environment switch for this call either, so the way back is another `kda_decode_backend`.

**Why `unique_or_null`.** vLLM's KDA metadata fills CUDA-graph padding rows with `NULL_BLOCK_ID` (0), the reserved null block owned by no request, and every live T=1 decode row owns its own block, so the state indices are non-positive or unique. FlashInfer treats non-positive rows as the null path (zero output, no state update). `positive_unique` would be a false assertion under padding. Because FlashInfer does not verify the mode on the device, it has to hold for every caller path that reaches the FlashInfer decode; the single call site in `_forward` is that path and it only runs for pure T=1 decode batches (`num_prefills == 0`, no speculative tokens).

issue_comments.body: Hi @yyihuang why does vLLM need to be aware of Cake? It would be nice if this was handled under the existing flashinfer api and dispatched based on autotuner shapes

Thanks @mgoin, fair question. Agreed that the end state is FlashInfer choosing these kernels itself, with nothing Cake-specific in vLLM. Why this PR carries a switch today, per call site (FlashInfer `main` as of b5e50c20):

* `fused_kda_decode`: the released default is `backend="cute-dsl"`. FlashInfer already has `backend="auto"`, which selects the Cake kernel only for the contract it covers (equal-head / D128 / T=1, `state_indices_mode` supplied) and keeps CuTe-DSL otherwise. So for this call the Cake-agnostic form exists: pass `backend="auto"` plus the host-known `state_indices_mode` and let FlashInfer decide. I can make the KDA layer do that unconditionally if you are fine with vLLM's KDA decode moving from the explicit `"cute-dsl"` default to FlashInfer's `"auto"`.
* `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`: `backend="auto"` resolves to the existing trtllm-gen kernels; the Cake FP8 MLA decode is only reachable through the explicit `backend="cake"`, and FlashInfer raises rather than falling back when the call does not match a generated program, which is why the shape predicate sits on the vLLM side. Dispatching it from `auto` / the autotuner is FlashInfer-side work; I will raise it there. The same holds for a GDN-prefill counterpart I have ready (`backend="cake_gdn"` is explicit; `auto` keeps FlashInfer's default kernel).

So the switch is a way to run and compare these kernels end to end in vLLM before FlashInfer promotes them, and the numbers in the description are the evidence for whether promotion is warranted at all. If you would rather not carry a Cake-specific knob in the meantime, two options: (a) drop `VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES` and this PR, pursue the `auto` promotion in FlashInfer, and come back with no vLLM change (or only the `backend="auto"` KDA change); (b) keep an engine-side knob but make it generic, e.g. a per-call-site FlashInfer backend override that just forwards `backend=` to the existing calls and validates nothing FlashInfer does not. Which would you prefer? I will hold the GDN-prefill PR until this is settled.

> (a) drop VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES and this PR, pursue the auto promotion in FlashInfer, and come back with no vLLM change (or only the backend="auto" KDA change)

I prefer this. And we should confirm switching to `backend="auto"` doesn't cause any perf or accuracy degradation.

Agreed, and thanks for pushing on this. I have dropped `VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES` and everything Cake-specific from this PR (head is now the reduced form).

What remains: when `kda_decode_backend="flashinfer"` is selected, the existing `fused_kda_decode` call passes `backend="auto"` plus the host-known `state_indices_mode="unique_or_null"` (CUDA-graph padding rows are null slots, live decode rows own their blocks), on FlashInfer builds that accept those kwargs (>= 0.7.1rc5; a signature probe keeps the call unchanged on the pinned 0.7.0.post1). FlashInfer then selects the kernel itself; vLLM's default KDA path is untouched.

The MLA change is dropped from this PR; making FlashInfer's `auto` / autotuner cover that kernel is FlashInfer-side work I will pursue there. Description updated; end-to-end numbers for this form will follow before I ask for review.

@mgoin on this head vLLM has no Cake awareness any more: the `VLLM_CAKE_ROUTES` switch, the admission predicates and the MLA route are gone (net diff: four files); the KDA layer passes `backend="auto"` + `state_indices_mode="unique_or_null"` when the installed FlashInfer accepts them (0.7.1rc1 and later) and FlashInfer picks the kernel, which the JIT lines below confirm.

@gau-nernst the end-to-end check of that form is in (announcement-fix revision 17c710419; the head since adds only a docstring correction); the description carries the full validation section, the short version:

**Setup.** `nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4` (served from a local copy), TP8 over two GB300 nodes (SM103), vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d nightly (cu134), FlashInfer built from `main` at flashinfer-ai/flashinfer@9eb882ad346d8ec8a18dca2f1cba4c7095b740c9 (has `backend` / `state_indices_mode`); `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --distributed-executor-backend ray --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --trust-remote-code --attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"mla_prefill_backend":"flashinfer"}'`. Two `vllm serve` arms on the same image, build and checkpoint: **native** (vLLM's own KDA decode) and **fiauto** (`--additional-config '{"kda_decode_backend":"flashinfer"}'`, i.e. `fused_kda_decode(backend="auto", state_indices_mode="unique_or_null")`). One run per arm, so differences below a few percent are noise.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, all 1319 test questions (a port of sglang's `few_shot_gsm8k` to `/v1/completions`: 5 shots, greedy, 512 max new tokens, last-integer scoring), 64-way concurrency: native **0.945**, fiauto **0.943** (unparseable 0.1 % / 0.2 %), 0 request errors in either arm. That is 2 to 3 questions from one greedy run per arm; the two kernels accumulate differently, so token-identical output is not expected, and I did not run repeats to put a band on it.

**Serving** (`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`, 1024-token prompts, 128 output tokens unless stated; median / p99 ms):

| scenario | arm | req/s | out tok/s | TTFT med / p99 | TPOT med / p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 prompts, concurrency 32 | native | 7.10 | 909 | 797 / 1337 | 27.30 / 31.49 |
|  | fiauto | 7.05 | 902 | 796 / 1330 | 27.45 / 31.70 |
| 32 prompts, concurrency 8 | native | 3.22 | 413 | 506 / 553 | 15.47 / 17.72 |
|  | fiauto | 3.24 | 415 | 505 / 535 | 15.40 / 17.60 |
| 8 prompts, concurrency 1 | native | 0.611 | 78.2 | 225 / 256 | 11.06 / 11.12 |
|  | fiauto | 0.615 | 78.7 | 223 / 231 | 11.05 / 11.11 |
| 4 × 8192-token prompts, 16 output, concurrency 1 | native | 1.85 | 29.6 | 351 / 419 | 11.40 / 11.63 |
|  | fiauto | 1.84 | 29.4 | 352 / 428 | 11.57 / 11.72 |

Throughput, median TTFT and median / p99 TPOT are within ±1.5 % of native in every scenario (largest +1.48 %, the 8192-token TPOT median; the warm-up pass in the description behaves the same); p99 TTFT moves by −3.1 % at concurrency 8, −9.7 % at concurrency 1 and +2.1 % for the 8192-token prompts, single-run tail values over 4 to 32 requests (deltas from the unrounded values). With one run per arm: no regression signal, and no measurable end-to-end gain at these shapes either (the KDA decode's share of the per-token time was not profiled).

**Which kernel ran.** The fiauto server log has 32 FlashInfer `Generated Cake fused KDA decode <variant> sm103a JIT spec` lines for four fp32-state variants (one set per rank by count), i.e. `auto` selected and compiled them at first use; the native log has none and no `fused_kda_decode` mention at all. A kernel-level probe on B200 (in the description) shows `auto` picking a Cake variant for all 11 shapes tried with the bf16-state inputs of the GPU correctness test (`test_kda.py`; H = 12 to 96, 1 and 4 rows, padded and contiguous strides), each within the BF16 tolerance of vLLM's reference.

One fix came out of this: the first run died while constructing the KDA layers because the once-only announcement passed a dict to `logger.info_once`, which hashes its arguments. The announcement-fix commit (17c710419) renders the kwargs to a string first and adds a CPU test that calls the real logger; the fiauto numbers above are from the rerun on that revision, the native arm ran on the revision before it (they differ only in the announcement helpers and their test); the head since adds only a docstring correction.

Given that e2e results don't show noticeable improvements, I'm not inclined to approve the PR given its pretty large changes. There are many unnecessary changes which I believe came from your agent, such as the `inspect` hack (we always pin FlashInfer version, so the inspection is unnecessary. Just validate with whatever FlashInfer version is pinned in vLLM).
